text:
Harper Zhou: quick RFC follow-up. i've been thinking about making observability first-class in our precision/profile contract. current problem: when a profile change (fp8->int8 or head-level int4) affects quality we often only discover it after customer reports. proposal: require three observability hooks on every profile variant: fingerprint, stable cache-key, and a minimal golden-check digest.
Miguel Alvarez: +1. can you define "golden-check digest"?
Harper Zhou: cheap summary signal we compute at deploy-time and emit with traces. e.g., run 64 tiny prompts that capture hallucination/answer-type behavior and store a small digest (embedding centroid + token-likelihood-summary). runtime can compare online results vs digest to detect drift.
Sofia Becker: that sounds useful. how do we keep it fast? don't want per-request heavy checks.
Harper Zhou: not per-request. emit it during canary evaluations and as a periodic background probe. probes run in sampling mode (1/1000 req or background cron). main idea: when fingerprint changes, generate candidate_digest and baseline_digest and produce a cheap divergence score. if divergence > threshold, flag candidate.
Kai O.: runtime pieces: we need a stable cache-key algorithm so caches don't thrash when we materialize resolved profiles. propose: cache_key = sha256(normalize(base_id) + '|' + sorted(patch_ids).join(',') + '|' + fingerprint). keep normalized strings short. example pseudo:

```
// pseudo
key = sha256(`${baseId}:${patchIds.sort().join(',')}:${fingerprint}`)
```

Miguel Alvarez: telemetry/alerts: emit event `quant.profile.candidate_evaluated` with payload tags {endpoint, tenant, candidate_id, baseline_fingerprint, divergence_score}. then an alert rule watches divergence_score by endpoint > X. also emit `quant.profile.fallback` when runtime substitutes a lower-fidelity profile.
Sofia Becker: QA/ops: we should define acceptable thresholds per workload class. conversational assistants might have tighter thresholds than embedding-only endpoints. also need a rollback window where we keep previous resolved_key pinned for quick fallback.
Harper Zhou: agree. suggested rollout behavior:
- any profile change creates candidate_id and candidate_digest
- route small % to candidate in canary, run golden probes and embeddings drift checks
- if pass, promote candidate to resolved_key and emit promotion event
- if fail, auto-throttle and pin endpoint to last_good_resolved_key and create incident ticket

Kai O.: add lint in CI that blocks profile changes without a candidate_digest present. also require owner field on profile/policy objects for oncall paging.
Miguel Alvarez: we also need to capture per-layer/heads changes in telemetry. if a patch only touches heads 4-6, the digest should include prompts that exercise those heads (we can annotate golden prompts with target head tags).
Sofia Becker: ops note: include a tiny canary harness that can be invoked from console for customer-specific patches. i.e., allow customer-eng to run golden-suite for their tenant before we push.
Harper Zhou: security: patches must be tenant-scoped and we should forbid non-tenant-owned patches from referencing private base profiles. verify in api layer.
Miguel Alvarez: implementation tasks:
- telemetry: add `quant.profile.candidate_evaluated`, `quant.profile.promoted`, `quant.profile.fallback`, `quant.profile.divergence_hist` metrics
- runtime: stable cache-key impl + fallback counter emittor
- infra: store candidate_digest in profile_store with small size limits (e.g., 4KB)
- QA: golden prompt sets per workload bucket and a head-annotated subset for head-level patches

Kai O.: infra-bot scheduled a canary run for prototype harness at 1765433348 :gear:
infra-bot: canary-harness: started job 1765433348 for cluster canary-3

Sofia Becker: i'll compose the workload buckets (chat, search, summarization, embedding) and PR the golden sets. Harper please add a short addendum to the RFC with the digest schema (embedding centroid + token-likelihood histogram + seed prompts ids).
Harper Zhou: will do. i'll also prototype the cheap divergence metric (cosine distance on centroids + KL on likelihood bins).
Miguel Alvarez: once we have metrics, we can wire an alert: divergence_score > 0.15 AND fallback_rate < 0.05 => page. if fallback_rate high, prefer auto-rollback.
Sofia Becker: assign: Miguel telemetry + alerting, Kai runtime cache-key + fallback emitter, Harper digest + addendum, me QA + golden-sets.
Harper Zhou: thanks all. i'll post the addendum link here when ready and open a follow-up for the lint-rule. closing thread for now.
